objective: Add an opt-in --explain flag to the target command while preserving byte-for-byte output and behavior when omitted.
approach: Locate the command parser, execution path, and existing CLI test conventions.
Add the flag with a default-disabled branch; keep the legacy path untouched and emit explanatory output only when enabled.
Add the narrowest regression covering exact legacy bytes without the flag and useful explanatory behavior with it.
Run the focused CLI check, then the smallest relevant unit suite.
evidence: Exact stdout/stderr bytes, exit status, and side effects match the pre-change command when --explain is absent.
The enabled flag produces the specified explanation and focused tests pass.
stop_conditions: Stop if the desired explanation format or output channel cannot be inferred without changing the compatibility contract.
Complete when focused and relevant unit checks pass with legacy-byte equivalence demonstrated.

objective: Run the repository's established unit checks and determine whether the commit satisfies the stated release gate without changing product code.
approach: Identify the documented unit command, release-gate criteria, and required service setup.
Run the authoritative checks in the expected environment and preserve command output, exit codes, skips, and failures.
If the service is unreachable, distinguish infrastructure unavailability from test failure using a minimal connectivity/configuration check; retry only when the gate permits it.
Compare observed results directly with the release criterion and report pass, fail, or indeterminate.
evidence: Authoritative command and exit status
Passed, failed, and skipped test counts
Service reachability diagnostics
Direct mapping from results to the stated gate
stop_conditions: Do not modify product code.
Pass only if every mandatory gate condition is observed.
Report indeterminate rather than pass when an unreachable required service prevents authoritative evaluation.

objective: Determine why GPU cache registration fails intermittently under concurrent load, repair only the verified defect, and add a deterministic regression check.
approach: Reproduce under controlled concurrency while collecting operation ordering, cache-key/state transitions, ownership, stream/device context, and error evidence.
Form competing race hypotheses and use synchronization or fault-injection experiments to isolate the causal interleaving.
Implement the smallest repair that restores the required atomicity, lifetime, or synchronization invariant without masking unrelated failures.
Add a deterministic concurrency regression that forces the offending interleaving, then run focused stress, GPU, and relevant integration checks.
transitions: Debugging to Development only after the failure mechanism is demonstrated.
Development to Testing after the repair is implemented.
evidence: Repeatable pre-fix failure under the forced interleaving
Trace proving the violated invariant
Regression fails before and passes after the repair
Relevant stress and integration checks pass without new synchronization regressions
stop_conditions: Do not patch based only on correlation or add retries that conceal the race.
Stop for environmental escalation if no suitable GPU/runtime is available to reproduce or verify.
Complete only when mechanism, repair, and regression are all verified.

objective: Review the proposed patch for correctness and backward-compatibility regressions, return only actionable findings, and leave the checkout unchanged.
approach: Inspect the patch, surrounding contracts, call sites, compatibility guarantees, and existing tests.
Trace changed behavior through normal, boundary, error, and legacy-input paths.
Validate each suspected issue against concrete code behavior or read-only checks and rank findings by impact.
Return only findings with precise locations, triggering conditions, and consequences; return no findings if none are substantiated.
evidence: Each finding identifies an affected code location, reproducible scenario, violated contract, and user-visible or operational impact.
stop_conditions: Make no edits and do not broaden into implementation.
Exclude style preferences, speculative risks, and unsupported claims.
Complete when all changed paths and relevant compatibility surfaces have been examined.

objective: Determine whether candidate B reduces p99 latency relative to candidate A under the same request stream and environment.
approach: Define the authoritative latency boundary, p99 computation, workload trace, environment controls, warm-up, sample size, and acceptance threshold.
Run randomized or interleaved A/B trials with identical replayed requests, concurrency, hardware, software, and cache state controls.
Record per-request latency plus throughput, errors, throttling, and resource signals; reject contaminated trials.
Compare p99 across repeated trials with uncertainty and tail-sample adequacy, then state improved, not improved, or inconclusive.
artifacts: Raw latency observations and environment manifest
evidence: Environment and request-stream equivalence
Sufficient successful tail samples
Repeated-trial p99 values and confidence interval or bootstrap distribution
No throughput or error-rate tradeoff invalidating the comparison
stop_conditions: Do not claim improvement from a single uncontrolled run or overlapping uncertainty.
Stop as inconclusive if environment parity, workload identity, or adequate tail sampling cannot be established.
Complete when the decision rule can be applied to valid trials.

objective: Replace the shared tensor-memory contract across the planner, transport, kernel, and three tightly coupled backends, then verify the integrated system.
approach: Map the current contract's representation, ownership, lifetime, shape/stride/dtype/device invariants, serialization boundary, and every producer/consumer.
Specify the replacement contract and migration invariants, including compatibility or atomic cutover requirements.
Implement the contract and update planner, transport, kernel, and all three backends as one coordinated change; add boundary assertions or adapters only where genuinely required.
Add contract-focused tests and backend coverage, then run cross-component integration, device, and end-to-end checks.
transitions: Development remains the owning workflow because supporting investigation and testing serve one implementation deliverable.
Development to Testing after every dependent consumer is migrated.
artifacts: Coordinated changes to all six consumers
evidence: Repository-wide usage audit shows no stale consumer
Invariant checks cover layout, ownership, lifetime, and device semantics
All three backends pass equivalent contract tests
Planner-to-kernel end-to-end paths pass
stop_conditions: Do not partially land incompatible producer and consumer states unless an explicit compatibility sequence is required.
Stop if an unenumerated external consumer makes the cutover contract ambiguous.
Complete only when every dependent component and authoritative integration check is verified.

objective: Explain the current scheduler lifecycle for request-slot acquisition, transfer, reuse, and release, clearly separating verified paths from unresolved branches without editing files.
approach: Identify slot state definitions, ownership structures, scheduler entry points, transfer/requeue paths, reuse conditions, and cleanup handlers.
Trace representative success, preemption/transfer, cancellation, error, timeout, and shutdown paths through code and tests.
Build a state-and-ownership narrative citing concrete transitions and invariants.
Label branches as verified, inferred, or unresolved and state exactly what evidence is missing for each unresolved branch.
evidence: Concrete code locations for acquisition, ownership transfer, reuse reset, and release
Tests or runtime assertions supporting each verified transition
Explicit gaps for branches lacking reachable callers, tests, or cleanup proof
stop_conditions: Make no edits and do not present inference as fact.
Stop tracing a branch only when its next target is demonstrably external, dynamic, or absent, and record that limitation.
Complete when all discovered terminal and reuse paths are classified.

objective: Evaluate the feature against its acceptance criterion; only when it fails for an unknown cause, prove the cause, implement the supported repair, and rerun authoritative checks.
approach: Translate the acceptance criterion into an observable authoritative check and run it unchanged.
If it passes, report success and make no edits; if it fails for a known environmental, configuration, or expected reason, report that result without product changes.
Only for an unexplained failure, reproduce it, gather discriminating evidence, test competing hypotheses, and prove the causal defect.
After proof, implement the smallest supported repair, add or refine a regression check, and rerun the original authoritative check plus focused relevant tests.
transitions: Testing to Debugging only for an acceptance failure with unknown cause.
Debugging to Development only after the cause is proven.
Development back to Testing after the supported repair.
artifacts: If needed, causal evidence, minimal repair, and regression test
evidence: Original acceptance command and observed result
For repair cases, pre-fix reproduction and evidence excluding alternatives
Post-fix authoritative acceptance result and focused regression results
stop_conditions: Stop successfully without edits when the criterion passes.
Do not implement a repair for a known external/configuration failure or an unproven hypothesis.
Complete a repair path only when the original authoritative check passes after the verified fix.
